# cato_dhcp_settings (Resource)

Manages existing account DHCP settings via networkConfig.dhcp. Destroy only removes Terraform ownership; remote settings are retained. Requires NCS_DHCP_PUBLIC_API.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cato_dhcp_settings" "example" {
  lease_time    = 3600
  relay_enabled = false
  # relay_timeout  = 10
  # relay_group_id = cato_dhcp_relay_group.example.id
}
# Enabled relay needs a timeout and group; omitted values retain existing config.
# Destroy removes Terraform ownership and retains account DHCP settings.
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `lease_time` (Number) DHCP lease duration in seconds (minimum 60).
- `relay_enabled` (Boolean) Enable DHCP relay. Enabling requires an effective group and timeout.

### Optional

- `relay_group_id` (String) Opaque standalone relay group ID. Omission preserves selection; disable relay to stop using it.
- `relay_timeout` (Number) Relay timeout in seconds (0–90). Omission preserves existing value; cannot be cleared.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier. Collection item IDs are opaque and must be preserved unchanged.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cato_dhcp_settings.example ACCOUNT_ID
```
